candidates.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash dsv4_topk Triton illegal memory access under high concurrency on H20; mitigated by max_num_seqs=256
candidates.snippet: ### Summary  When serving `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90), I can hit a CUDA illegal memory access in the Triton `dsv4_topk` MoE routing kernel under high concurrency when `max_num_seqs` is configured above 256.  Reducing `max_num_seqs` to `256` makes the deployment stable and the crash is no longer reproducible under the same workload. candidates.snippet: ## Describe the bug  The GDN packed decode kernel computes the beta gate as follows.  ```python # python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_recurrent.py:255 beta_val = tl.sigmoid(b_val).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32) ```  `tl.sigmoid` is evaluated in fp32, the result is rounded to the input dtype (bf16 in serving), then cast back to fp32. candidates.title: Cloud models wedge after ~45 min on 0.34.0 (502, no error); 0.33.1 works
candidates.snippet: ## What happens  Cloud models wedge after about 45 minutes of serving on 0.34.0. The same account and the same model work fine on 0.33.1.  `deepseek-v4-pro:cloud` responds normally for a while (2 to 8 seconds per request). Then latency climbs steadily. 16s, 17s, 28s. Then one request hangs for 4m15s. After that every request returns 502.  The server log shows the degradation curve and the 502s, but no underlying error. `POST /api/generate` receives the request and never sends back an HTTP status
